chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Fuḍayl ibn Sukkarah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “May I be sacrificed for you, is there a fixed limit for the water with which the deceased is washed?”
He said: “Indeed, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘When I die, draw six waterskins of water from the well of Ghars, then wash me, shroud me, and embalm me.’”

‘Then when you have finished washing me and shrouding me, take hold of the whole of my shroud and sit me up; then ask me whatever you wish, for by Allah, you will not ask me about anything except that I will answer you regarding it.’”

key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water used for the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person to be washed and prepared for burial
key_terms.بِئْرِ غَرْسٍ: the well of Ghars from which the water was to be drawn
key_terms.حَدٌّ مَحْدُودٌ: a fixed, specified limit or measure
key_terms.سِتَّ قِرَبٍ: six waterskins drawn as the amount mentioned in the report
key_terms.فَغَسِّلْنِي: wash me; perform the ghusl of the deceased
key_terms.وَحَنِّطْنِي: embalm me with ḥunūṭ for burial preparation
key_terms.وَكَفِّنِّي: shroud me in the funeral shroud

ai.seo_question: Is there a fixed amount of water prescribed for washing the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question about whether there is a fixed quantity of water for washing the deceased, and the Imam عليه السلام answers by citing the instruction of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله to Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام. It also conveys a distinctive report about the final rites of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his promise to answer ʿAlī عليه السلام after his washing and shrouding.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Fuzayl Bin Sukrat who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Is there a restrictive limit for the water which the deceased is washed with?’

He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>: ‘When I<sup>saww</sup> pass away, so draw six pitchers of water of a well of Ghars, so wash me<sup>saww</sup>, and enshroud me<sup>saww</sup>, and embalm me<sup>saww</sup>.

So when you<sup>asws</sup> are free from washing me<sup>saww</sup> and enshrouding me<sup>asws</sup>, so grab me<sup>saww</sup> with the entirety of my<sup>saww</sup> shroud and sit me<sup>saww</sup> up, then ask me<sup>saww</sup> about whatever you<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, you<sup>asws</sup> will not ask me<sup>saww</sup> about anything except that I<sup>saww</sup> would answer you<sup>asws</sup> with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Fudayl (ibn) Sukkarah who has said that he said to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) the following.
“‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, is there a certain quantitiyof water required to give Ghusl (bath) a dead person?”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “The Messenger of Allah said to Ali (a.s.), ‘When I will die draw six sacks of water from the well Ghars (name of the well). Then wash my body, shroud it and rub camphor on my forehead, palms, knees and toes.

When you finish washing my body and shrouding hold by the ends of the shroud and set my body in a sitting posture then ask me whatever you would like. I swear by Allah, you would not ask me anything but that I will give you an answer in it.”
